newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt says stocks unlikely to plunge.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt says stocks unlikely to plunge.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are unlikely to fall drastically and the Japanese government wants the prices to move in a stable manner, Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference on Tuesday.
"Stocks remained soft, but I have a feeling (the price decline) will not be very drastic...I want a stable attitude (in the market)," Kajiyama said.
Tokyo stocks struggled back up above the 20,000 level by midday Tuesday after dipping below that key level earlier, the first time the Nikkei has been below 20,000 since March 15, brokers said.
At midday, the benchmark Nikkei 225 average was up 88.73 points or 0.44 percent to 20,195.84, off a low of 19,920.02. Its September futures were up 60 points to 20,210.
